topics.label: Introduction to complement
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement system, outlining its importance and setting up the lecture.

topics.label: Foundations, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide the foundational overview of the complement cascade, explain its naming conventions, and establish C3 as the central reaction hub.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct upstream pathways that recognize pathogens, form convertases, and drive complement to its activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream mechanisms by which activated complement eliminates pathogens and stimulates an immune response.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that prevent complement from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct disease presentations and infection susceptibilities resulting from deficiencies in various complement components and regulators.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the strategies evolved by pathogens to neutralize complement activity and survive immune attack.

topics.label: Conclusion and next lecture preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session on complement and provides a brief forward look to the upcoming lecture on adaptive immunity.
